Patient: Scott Castro

Discharge Date: 10/21/2022
Attending Physician: Dr. Anthony Thomas, Nephrology

Principal Diagnosis:
Proteinuria (urine protein 260 mg/dL)

Secondary Diagnoses:
None

Hospital Course:
Mr. Scott Castro, a 36-year-old male, was admitted on October 19, 2022, with a primary diagnosis of proteinuria. The patient was referred for evaluation after a routine urine test revealed elevated protein levels. Upon admission, his blood pressure was 135/71 mmHg and his weight was recorded at 140 pounds.

During the hospital stay, Mr. Castro underwent a series of diagnostic tests to evaluate the cause of proteinuria. These tests included a comprehensive metabolic panel, renal ultrasound, and a 24-hour urine collection for protein quantification. The 24-hour urine collection confirmed proteinuria with a urine level of 260 mg/dL. Further workup did not reveal any significant abnormalities, and the proteinuria was deemed to be controlled.

Mr. Castro's hospital course was uneventful. He was monitored closely, and his vital signs remained stable throughout his stay. No acute interventions were required, and he was discharged home in stable condition on October 21, 2022.

Discharge Medications:
None. Mr. Castro was advised to continue with his current medications and follow-up with his primary care physician ongoing management of his condition.

Social History:
Mr. Castro is a former smoker, having quit cigarettes on September 3, 2024. He previously smoked half a pack per starting from March 26, 2015. He consumes approximately 46 alcoholic drinks per week.

Family History:
The patient's mother has a history of type 2 diabetes, diagnosed at age 69. She is currently 90 years old and living.

Follow-Up:
Mr. Castro is scheduled to follow up with Dr. Anthony Thomas in the nephrology clinic on February 9, 2026. He was instructed to monitor his blood pressure at home and maintain a healthy diet. He was also advised to reduce his alcohol intake and continue abstaining from tobacco use.

Vital Signs on Discharge:
Blood Pressure: 132/76 mmHg
Weight: 153 pounds

Discharge Instructions:
- Continue to monitor blood pressure at home.
- Follow a low-sodium diet.
- Reduce alcohol consumption.
- Attend follow-up appointments as scheduled.
